title: A Bird Builds Its Nest From Spit, and People Pay $2,000 a Kilo for It

scenes.text: A bird spits for 35 days. Then someone eats it.
The edible-nest swiftlet, 15 grams, lives in pitch-black caves in Borneo and finds its way by clicking, like a bat.
The male builds the nest from strands of his own hardened saliva. No twigs, no leaves. It takes 35 days.
Harvesters climb bamboo scaffolds and 60-metre poles in the dark to peel them off the roof. Many have fallen to their deaths.
White nests sell for around 2,000 dollars a kilo. Rare red nests, up to 10,000. The global trade is worth billions.
Over 200 tons are eaten every year, mostly in China. It's spit. Thirty-five days of it.

description:
The edible-nest swiftlet builds its nest entirely from its own hardened saliva over about 35 days, inside pitch-black caves it navigates with echolocating clicks.
Harvesters climb bamboo scaffolds and 60-metre poles to collect the nests, which sell for around $2,000 a kilo (red nests up to $10,000) in a global bird's nest trade estimated at $8.5 billion, with over 200 tons eaten a year, mostly in China.
Would you try bird's nest soup?

first_comment: A swiftlet nest is about 62 percent protein, and a single chicken egg has as much protein as 26 bowls of the soup. Still worth $100 a bowl?
